care.title: Your flowers
care.intro: A few minutes now keeps them for a week or more.
steps: Trim each stem at an angle, about two centimetres, with a clean knife or scissors.
Fill a clean vase with cool water and the flower food in the card.
Strip any leaves that would sit below the water.
Keep them out of direct sun, away from radiators and away from the fruit bowl.
Change the water and trim again every two days.
care.lasts: Most of our arrangements last a week; garden roses and dahlias a little less, chrysanthemums much longer.

blocks.heading: Why one arrangement a week
blocks.body:
We make one arrangement each week from the best of the market and make it well. Everything else is made to order.

If you'd like something different, message us: we usually can.

deliveryAreas.title: Where we deliver
deliveryAreas.intro: By hand, from the studio in Pimlico, to these postcodes. Each has its own cut-off for same-day delivery and its own charge.

how.a: One of us, in the studio van. Never a courier.
We ring the number you give us. With your say-so we'll leave the flowers with a neighbour or a concierge; otherwise we bring them back and try again the same day.

how.q: Can you deliver at a set time?
how.a: We deliver between 10am and 5pm. For a morning or a set time, message us and we'll say honestly whether the van can.
Outside these postcodes we can't deliver by hand. Collect from the studio, or message us and we'll find a way.

notice.q: How much notice do you need?
notice.a: Two working days for a wreath or posy, five for a coffin spray. If the service is sooner, message us and we'll say honestly what we can do.

notice.q: Do you deliver to the funeral director?
notice.a: Yes, by hand, to any funeral director in the areas we deliver to: the day before or the morning of the service, whichever they prefer.
Whatever you'd like. We write it by hand. If words are hard, we can suggest a few.

notice.q: Can you use their favourite flowers or colours?
notice.a: Yes. Tell us what they loved and we'll build the piece around it, in season where we can.

stories.title: Our work
stories.intro: Weddings and events, one at a time: what we were asked for, the colours, the stems and how it looked on the day.

items.title: A June wedding in blush and white
items.line: Garden roses and sweet peas, with the church kept almost bare.
items.brief: The couple wanted the church to feel like a garden after rain: soft, scented and not too formal. The bride's dress was ivory silk, so we kept white away from her bouquet and let blush do the work.

contract.intro: Flowers for the rooms people walk into, changed every week before you open.
contract.weekly: Every Monday or Tuesday morning, before you open, we take away last week's flowers and bring in new ones from this week's market. The colours follow the season; the size, the vases and the places stay yours.

how.a: We visit, look at the rooms and the light, and send you a plan with the prices. The first week is the same price as every other.

how.q: Who looks after the flowers between visits?
how.a: We do. Water is topped up on the change day, and if anything tires mid-week we'll swap it.
Yes: more for an event, less in August, a colour for a launch. Message us by the Friday before.
A monthly invoice for the weeks we came. No minimum term after the first month.
